subject: Chemistry
scope: Eight short single-fact mock-eligible Year 1 Chemistry recall checks that did not appear as direct questions in the audited active core deck or previous chemistry mock supplements.
notes: Original AQA-style paraphrases, not past-paper text. Measurements questions are conceptual, not laboratory instructions. Task 1 is still incomplete.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the relative formula mass of an ionic compound?
cards.back: Sum of the relative atomic masses of the atoms in its formula unit.
accept: Sum of the relative atomic masses of the atoms in its formula unit.
Add the Ar values for the atoms in one formula unit.
Total of the relative atomic masses in the chemical formula.
Sum of Ar values, accounting for subscripts.
reject: The mass of a single molecule in grams.
The number of formula units in a mole.
The mass of one mole in g mol-1.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why is relative formula mass used instead of relative molecular mass for ionic compounds?
cards.back: Ionic compounds form extended lattices rather than discrete molecules.
accept: Ionic compounds form extended lattices rather than discrete molecules.
Ionic solids do not consist of separate molecules.
They are ionic lattices, not individual molecules.
Their formulae express the simplest ion ratio, not molecules.
reject: Each ionic compound consists of isolated molecules.
Because ionic compounds have no relative atomic masses.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Does relative atomic mass have a unit?
cards.back: No, it is a ratio and has no unit.
accept: No, it is a ratio and has no unit.
No units.
It is dimensionless.
No; it is a relative mass ratio.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What are the usual units of molar mass in mole calculations using grams?
accept: g mol⁻¹.
grams per mole
g/mol
g mol-1

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is water of crystallisation in a hydrated salt?
cards.back: Water present in a crystal lattice in a fixed formula ratio.
accept: Water present in a crystal lattice in a fixed formula ratio.
Water incorporated in a crystal structure in a fixed proportion.
Water molecules forming part of a hydrated crystal.
Water in the crystalline structure of a hydrated compound.
reject: Water added to dissolve a salt.
Water just on the surface of a damp sample.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: When multiplying or dividing measured quantities, what usually limits the significant figures in the answer?
cards.back: The measured input with the fewest significant figures.
accept: The measured input with the fewest significant figures.
The least precise measured value, by significant figures.
Use no more significant figures than the input with the fewest.
The smallest number of significant figures among measured inputs.
reject: The number with the most significant figures.
Always round to one significant figure.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What does accuracy mean for a measurement?
cards.back: Closeness to the true or accepted value.
accept: Closeness to the true or accepted value.
How near a measurement is to the true value.
Closeness to the accepted reference value.
How near a result is to the correct value.
reject: Closeness of repeated readings to one another.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What does precision describe for repeated measurements?
cards.back: How closely repeated measurements agree with each other.
accept: How closely repeated measurements agree with each other.
The closeness of repeat readings.
How little scatter repeated readings show.
How similar repeated measured values are.
reject: How accurately a theoretical value was predicted.
